en.title: 10 Must-See Films Arriving in October 2026
en.summary: Get ready for an explosion of cinematic brilliance this October, with documentaries, international gems, and compelling dramas hitting screens.
en.body:
October is here, and it's bringing an embarrassment of riches to the big screen and your streaming queues. Forget the cozy sweaters and pumpkin spice; this month is all about diving headfirst into a diverse and dazzling lineup of films that demand your attention.

## 1. Verity
Dakota Johnson stars in this highly anticipated film, set to premiere on October 2nd. Early buzz suggests a thought-provoking narrative that could redefine the genre.

## 2. The Social Reckoning
Arriving on October 2nd, this film has already generated significant buzz. It promises a timely examination of societal issues, making it a must-watch for anyone interested in contemporary narratives.

## 3. Other Mommy
Mark your calendars for October 9th, as 'Other Mommy' prepares to make its debut. This intriguing title is already drawing comparisons to acclaimed character studies, hinting at a deeply resonant experience.

## 4. Whalefall
Prepare for an aquatic adventure on October 16th with 'Whalefall.' This film is poised to be a visually stunning spectacle, offering a unique blend of nature and human drama.

## 5. Street Fighter
Fans of action and iconic characters, rejoice! 'Street Fighter' lands in theaters on October 16th, promising a high-octane adaptation that aims to capture the spirit of the beloved game franchise.

## 6. Klara and the Sun
Based on Kazuo Ishiguro's acclaimed novel, 'Klara and the Sun' arrives on October 23rd. Its exploration of artificial intelligence and human connection is expected to be a cinematic standout.

## 7. Wildwood
Another gem landing on October 23rd, 'Wildwood' is an animated feature that has critics buzzing. Its imaginative world-building and enchanting story are perfect for audiences of all ages.

## 8. La Bola Negra
Premiering in theaters October 16th before hitting Netflix December 2nd, Los Javis' 'La Bola Negra' is a bold, novelistic thriller that captivated audiences at Cannes. Its intricate narrative structure, described as an 'impressive jigsaw,' invites viewers to decode its layered meanings, echoing modernist literary techniques.

## 9. Closure
Michal Marczak returns with 'Closure' on October 28th, a documentary that blurs the lines between reality and fiction. This Grand Jury Prize winner at Sundance follows a father's poignant search for his missing son, boasting cinematography that rivals narrative features.

## 10. Wicker
Alex Huston Fischer and Eleanor Wilson's 'Wicker,' arriving October 23rd, is set to be a unique love story. Starring Olivia Colman, this fable-like film promises a fresh perspective on romance and relationships.
Bottom Line: This October, prepare for a cinematic feast with diverse stories that range from thrilling action to profound human dramas.

content_raw: As we go deeper into fall, the most impressive month of the year for new releases is here. Featuring no shortage of staggering, essential documentaries, as well as a few of the best international films of the year, it’s an embarrassment of cinematic riches. So much so that a Palme d’Or winner and certain action star’s return to drama didn’t even make the main cut. 13. La Bola Negra (Los Javis, Oct. 16 in theaters and Dec. 2 on Netflix) A jolt to the Cannes Film Festival when it premiered later in the lineup, Los Javis’ La Bola Negra was snapped up by Netflix, which will roll it out in their longest theatrical window yet. Jan Tracz said in his review , “The film also joins a lineage of contemporary cinema that aspires to novelistic storytelling through audiovisual means. Last year’s  Sound of Falling  had a similar premise, echoing influential modernist writers like Virginia Woolf and William Faulkner to create a provocative stream of consciousness through images rather than literature. Here, the ‘cinema of attractions’ resembles the style of Mario Vargas Llosa’s 1969 novel  Conversation in the Cathedral , each sequence adding another layer of meaning to the equation. It is for the spectator to decide when and how they will decode this impressive jigsaw.” 12. Closure (Michal Marczak; Oct. 28) After first landing on my radar with the wondrous All These Sleepless Nights , Michal Marczak returned this year with another film blending the realms of fact and fiction. Closure , a documentary that is better shot than most narrative films this year, follows a father trying to track down his missing son. A Grand Jury Prize winner at Sundance and top winner at Thessaloniki Documentary Festival 2026, it’ll now arrive before the end of October. 11. Wicker (Alex Huston Fischer and Eleanor Wilson, Oct. 23) A love story unlike any this year, Alex Huston Fischer & Eleanor Wilson’s Wicker tells a fable in which a woman (Olivia Colman) commissions a wicker husband (Alexander Skarsgård) to be made by the local basketmaker (Peter Dinklage). As Kent M. Wilhelm said in his Sundance review of the film also starring Elizabeth Debicki and shot by Lol Crawley ( The Brutalist ), “This sophomore feature is a lighthearted period piece set in a time and place that never existed. Their screenplay, based on Ursula Wills-Jones’s short story The Wicker Husband , is a skewering of patriarchal relationship dynamics and traditions. The world they construct is a fun house mirror’s reflection of reality, allowing for a heightened world that feels believable despite its anachronous qualities.” 10.
